strengths: A genuinely organising framework (math versus mirror) with an audit per clip.
Most arithmetic reproduces and the corrections are usually fair.
Calls out two disguised advertisements and the recursive funnel pattern.
weaknesses: Two miscast figures (monthly daylight, the $20,000 a month).
The closing "rule" is announced and then only restates the preceding line.
Thumbnail clips are not the clips discussed.
The source of the headline statistic is unnamed.
contradictions: "Five figures of monthly daylight" versus about $5,000-$6,500 left.
"$20,000 a month comes in" versus the caller's $13,600.
Opening promise to "tell the difference in seconds" versus no explicit closing test.
"The exact same two-week runway as everyone else in this video" names a runway no clip states.
improvement_opportunities: State the one-line math-versus-mirror test explicitly on screen at the end (for example, "if one fixed cost explains more than half the gap it is math; if the gap has no line item it is a mirror").
Correct the $20,000 to the caller's $13,600 and the monthly-versus-annual slip.
Use two of the actual clips in the thumbnail or retitle the thumbnail text to match.
Add a subscribe ask after the first audited clip and a next-video pointer.
